cleanIntro: This guide follows MasterPiece Arms' manual for the MPA BA rifle family; check your variant against it. The book never names the BA Comp Pro, so every step here is stated as generally as the book states it. It is a bolt-action rifle on a chassis, and the only part the book has an owner take off is the bolt. ⛔ Everything past that, the trigger included, goes to a gunsmith or back to MasterPiece Arms.

steps.title: Safety fully back to S before anything else
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and pull the safety fully to the rear, to the S mark. The book asks for S before the rifle is handled, loaded or unloaded, so it comes first here. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time: the book is plain that even on S, careless handling can still make the rifle fire.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, pull the safety mechanism fully to the rear towards the ‘S’ position. Always put the safety mechanism in the ‘S’ position before handling, loading or unloading the firearm.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — The Safety, PDF p.4 (the book prints no page numbers)

steps.title: Hand over the port, then draw the bolt back slowly
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle. Cup one hand over the top of the ejection port and draw the bolt back slowly with the other. A round in the chamber comes out into your hand instead of flying across the bench. Going slowly also lets you feel the round come free rather than guess.
steps.quote: Put one hand over the top of the ejection port. 5. Slowly pull the bolt handle rearward with your other hand to remove the cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — To Unload the Firearm, PDF p.6

steps.title: Magazine out, and empty it
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and take the magazine box out. Then empty it, cartridge by cartridge, and put the rounds away from the rifle. A magazine that goes back in still loaded is how a cleared rifle gets loaded again.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine catch to release magazine box. 7. Remove all cartridges from the magazine box.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — To Unload the Firearm, PDF p.6

steps.title: Look in the chamber and the magazine before going on
steps.action: Look into the chamber and into the magazine. Both must be empty before anything else is done. If you are not sure about either one, go back to the start of this section rather than carrying on.
steps.quote: WARNING! Check the chamber and the magazine to make sure there are no cartridges in the firearm.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — To Unload the Firearm, PDF p.6

steps.title: Bolt handle up and all the way back
steps.action: With the safety still on S and your fingers away from the trigger, lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. It stops there against the bolt stop. It will not come out until the bolt stop release is pressed in the next step.
steps.quote: Do not touch the trigger while moving the safety mechanism. 4. Raise the bolt handle. 5. Pull the bolt handle all the way back.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — To Remove Bolt Assembly, PDF p.4

steps.title: Press the bolt stop release on the left, and slide the bolt out
steps.action: The bolt stop release sits on the upper left side of the action, to the left of the bolt handle. Hold it in and slide the bolt straight out of the back of the receiver. Lay the bolt down clean, away from grit, while the barrel is worked on.
steps.quote: Push bolt stop release on the upper left side of the action – to the left of the bolt handle. 7. Slide the bolt assembly from the firearm.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — To Remove Bolt Assembly, PDF p.4

steps.title: Look down the bore from the chamber end
steps.action: With the bolt out, look through the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle. You are checking for anything in the bore before you start: mud, snow, grease, heavy oil or a stuck patch all count as an obstruction to the book.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt. 7. Look through the inside of the barrel from the chamber end to the muzzle.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — The Barrel: To check the inside of the barrel, PDF p.5

steps.title: Bolt out is as far as the book goes
steps.action: This is the whole owner strip. The book has an owner remove the bolt and nothing else. It sends trigger adjustment to the maker, and it sends servicing to a gunsmith or back to the factory. Nothing past the bolt is taken apart here.
steps.quote: Masterpiece Arms firearms should only be serviced by an authorized gunsmith or sent back to the factory.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Firearms Safety Procedures, rule 15, PDF p.2

steps.title: Clean through a bore guide, every time
steps.action: Fit a bore guide in the action before a rod goes anywhere near the barrel. The book is blunt about it: more barrels are ruined by cleaning rods than by shooting. The guide keeps the rod centred so it cannot rub the chamber neck or the throat.
steps.quote: More rifle barrels are destroyed by cleaning without a bore guide than by shooting!
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Barrel Care and Life: Barrel Brake In and Cleaning, PDF p.7

steps.title: Bore cleaner, then copper and carbon
steps.action: Work the bore with a good bore cleaner, then a copper fouling remover and a carbon fouling remover. The book names the three kinds of product, not brands. Run the rod from the chamber end, through the bore guide.
steps.quote: You want to use a good bore cleaner, copper fouling remover and carbon fouling remover.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Barrel Care and Life: Barrel Brake In and Cleaning, PDF p.7

steps.title: Check the work with a bore scope, chamber neck included
steps.action: Look down the bore with a bore scope if you have one. The book asks you to check that the copper and carbon are gone, and it names the neck of the chamber as the place carbon builds up.
steps.quote: We also recommend the use of a bore scope to inspect the inside of your barrel to ensure you have removed the copper fouling and carbon buildup (especially in the neck of the chamber).
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Barrel Care and Life: Barrel Brake In and Cleaning, PDF p.7

steps.title: Protect the crown
steps.action: Look at the crown at the muzzle for dings or gouges. A damaged crown costs accuracy. If you find one, the book sends the rifle to a gunsmith to put it right rather than having the owner touch it.
steps.quote: Always protect the Crown at the muzzle end of the barrel.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Crown, PDF p.7

steps.title: Protect the threads and the shoulder behind them
steps.action: The book's muzzle thread is 5/8-24 unless the rifle was ordered otherwise. Keep the threads and the machined shoulder behind them clean and covered with a thread protector or a muzzle device. The book says damage to either one affects accuracy with a device fitted.
steps.quote: It is highly recommended that you protect these threads and the shoulder behind the threads at all times.
steps.cite: MPA BA Rifle Manual — MPA-Bolt-Action-Rifle-Manual-1-24 (the maker's file name; the document prints no edition, date or page numbers) — Threaded Barrel, PDF p.6

deepAbsentReason: The MPA BA Rifle Manual prints no disassembly past removing the bolt (To Remove Bolt Assembly, PDF p.4). It sends trigger adjustment to the manufacturer (The Trigger Assembly, PDF p.4), refers barrel break-in and the action-screw method to videos (PDF pp.7-8), and says MasterPiece Arms firearms should only be serviced by an authorized gunsmith or sent back to the factory (PDF p.2). There is no deeper owner procedure in the book to quote.

cleaning.name: BEFORE YOU START
tasks: Clean only a rifle you have just cleared: safety on S, magazine out and empty, chamber seen empty, bolt out
Keep ammunition off the bench while you work
Wear eye protection when cleaning: the book warns of springs and solvents reaching the eyes

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore guide in the action before any rod
Rod from the chamber end, all the way through
Bore cleaner, copper fouling remover, carbon fouling remover
Check with a bore scope if you have one, chamber neck included
Do not try to shoot an obstruction out. If a rod will not push it out, the rifle goes to the factory or a gunsmith

cleaning.name: MUZZLE
tasks: Look at the crown for dings or gouges. A damaged crown goes to a gunsmith
Clean the threads and the shoulder behind them, then fit the thread protector or muzzle device

cleaning.name: BEFORE FIRING
tasks: Clean the bore and chamber of grease and oil before the rifle is fired
Do not alter the trigger or the safety. Trigger adjustment goes to MasterPiece Arms

reassembly: Safety on S, muzzle pointed somewhere safe.
Line up the lugs on the bolt with the receiver, slide the bolt in and push it all the way home.
Push the bolt handle down to close it.
Fit the thread protector or the muzzle device, run up to the shoulder behind the threads.
fncheck: With the rifle cleared (magazine out, chamber seen empty) and the muzzle somewhere safe: the bolt should slide fully in with its lugs lined up and close with the handle pushed down. The safety should pull fully back to S and push forward to F, and be left on S. Do not test it by pulling the trigger on S: the book says never to. Lift the handle and draw the bolt back: it must stop against the bolt stop and come out only with the release on the left side pressed. Anything else means the rifle goes to a gunsmith or back to MasterPiece Arms before it is loaded.
